import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 996

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
-/

open MeasureTheory AddCircle Filter Topology Asymptotics Finset Real

namespace Erdos996

noncomputable def fourierPartial {T : ℝ} [hT : Fact (0 < T)] (f : Lp ℂ 2 (@haarAddCircle T hT))
    (k : ℕ) : AddCircle T → ℂ :=
  fun x => ∑ i ∈ Icc (-k : ℤ) k, fourierCoeff f i • fourier i x

/-- Does there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `f ∈ L²[0,1]` and all lacunary
sequences `n`, if `‖f - fₖ‖₂ = O(1 / log log log k ^ C)`, then for almost every `x`,
`lim ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, f (n k • x)) / N = ∫ t, f t ∂t`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 42]
theorem erdos_996 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log (log k))) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle)) := by
  sorry

/-- The following theorem is proved in [Ma66]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 42]
theorem erdos_996.variants.log2 : ∀ (C : ℝ), 0.5 < C →
    ∀ (f : Lp ℂ 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    IsLacunary n →
    (fun k => (eLpNorm (⇑f - fourierPartial f k) 2 (haarAddCircle (T := 1))).toReal) =O[atTop]
    (fun k => 1 / (log (log k)) ^ C)
    →
    ∀ᵐ x, Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ .range N, f (n k • x)) / N) atTop
    (𝓝 (∫ t, f t ∂haarAddCircle)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos996

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement permits arbitrary finite prefixes, including zero terms, because IsLacunary requires the gap inequality only eventually. The sources use positive, globally lacunary sequences indexed from 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every Lean-lacunary sequence has a positive tail satisfying the gap inequality at every index. Removing a fixed finite prefix preserves a Cesàro limit: the discarded prefix contributes a fixed sum divided by N, and the change in normalization tends to 1. The Fourier-decay hypothesis is independent of the sequence, so this transformation preserves the same absolute exponent C. Conversely, positive global lacunarity implies IsLacunary. The full existential-C statement with these two sequence conditions was proved equivalent as Review996.main_shape_iff in /workspace/review/tail_equivalence.lean, without using the conjecture's sorry.

reformulations.difference: As in the main theorem, the Lean variant uses eventual lacunarity rather than requiring positive terms and the gap condition at every index.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each fixed C > 1/2, pass to a positive globally lacunary tail and use invariance of Cesàro convergence under deletion of a finite prefix. The double-logarithmic Fourier bound is unchanged because it does not involve the sequence. Global lacunarity gives the reverse implication immediately. The equivalence of the complete universally quantified variant was proved as Review996.log2_shape_iff in /workspace/review/tail_equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: Matsuyama states his corollary for real-valued, 1-periodic functions with mean zero and L² norm one; Lean allows arbitrary complex-valued L² functions and uses their integral as the limit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Subtracting the mean leaves every Fourier-tail error unchanged, since the partial sum includes the constant mode. Scaling a nonzero centered function to unit norm only changes the implied Big-O constant. Constant functions are immediate. For a complex function, symmetric Fourier truncation commutes with taking real and imaginary parts; each component's error norm is bounded by the complex error norm. Apply the real result to both components and intersect their full-measure sets. Conversely, the normalized real statement is a special case of the Lean formulation.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, On the strong law of large numbers, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 67 (1949), 51–56, especially pp. 51–52: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1949-09.pdf

N. Matsuyama, On the strong law of large numbers, Tohoku Math. J. (2) 18 (1966), 259–269, especially the definitions on p. 259 and corollary on p. 260: https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/tmj1949/18/3/18_3_259/_pdf
P. Erdős, Problems and results on diophantine approximations, Compositio Math. 16 (1964), 52–65, especially pp. 56–58: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-24.pdf

review.notes: All three declarations were checked; no mathematical defects or stale statuses were found. The source still records the main problem as open and attributes the C > 1/2 variant to Matsuyama. The AddCircle 1 formulation represents reduction modulo 1, and its default volume equals haarAddCircle. Lean checks proved that the Fourier-tail eLpNorm is finite before applying toReal, that every quantified f is integrable, and that the convergence property is independent of the chosen Lp representative. Boundary tests covered k = 0 through 3, zero functions, first Fourier modes, constant sequences, geometric lacunary sequences, and the harmless initial logarithm/division defaults. Both /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/tail_equivalence.lean compile without errors or warnings; the equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. No checkout files were edited.
